proof_summary: Set \(x=\varphi/5\) and \(y=\varphi^{-1}/5\), jointly order the three event families \(m,\ m/x,\ m/y\), and observe that the number of events up to \(T\) is \(\lfloor T\rfloor+\lfloor Tx\rfloor+\lfloor Ty\rfloor\), whose values at the three kinds of events are exactly the three sequence terms. Irrationality of \(x\), \(y\), and \(y/x\) prevents ties, while successive events increase this count by one, so their ranks exhaust the positive integers uniquely.
